statement: [unfavourable to AZD7545, neutral for DCA and VER-246608] Astrocytes are PDK4-dominant: mouse P7 Pdk4 63.70 against Pdk2 17.27 FPKM (2 pools); human mature astrocytes PDK4 22.59 against PDK2 7.52 (12 patients, 8-63 y); human snRNA astrocyte cluster PDK4 151.4 against PDK2 23.7 nCPM. Mouse adult astrocytes in the 2016 table show Pdk2 42.35 above Pdk4 9.45, so the mouse age course is not shown to match (different pipeline and batch). [V1 correction: the rise of PDK4 with maturation holds for human only; the mouse series in the same GEO table goes the other way (adult astrocytes Pdk2 above Pdk4)]

[mixed; species difference in the same lineage] Mouse oligodendrocyte lineage ranks Pdk2 first (OPC 16.62, newly formed 36.22, myelinating 33.23 FPKM), Pdk3 second (9.24, 20.88, 23.97) and Pdk4 near the floor (1.08, 0.48, 1.71). The PDK1/PDK2 rows of AZD7545 fit the mouse lineage better than the human one.

statement: [favourable but confounded] Rat pilocarpine seizure: PDK2 staining +83.1%, PDH -62.1%, phospho-PDHA1 Ser293 +62.3%, ATP -42.5% after seizure; DCA plus pyruvate reversed part of this and raised surviving neurons (CA1 +36.8%), while DCA alone or pyruvate alone did not raise neuron counts (n=8 per seizure group, 5 per sham group). Only the combination worked, so a PDK-inhibition-only effect is not shown. [V1 correction: n = 5 sham and 8 seizure holds for Methods and the behaviour panel; blot panels n = 3 or 4; staining panels n = 4 sham and 5-7 seizure; the percentages come from the blot and staining panels] [V2 correction: Fig 6 legend gives n = 4 per sham group and 5-7 per seizure group; the single-agent arms exist and only DCA plus pyruvate is significant (Fig 6 viewed by the verifier)]

[unfavourable: worsening documented at abstract level] In mouse seizure models DCA did not lengthen seizure latency (flurothyl), was slightly proconvulsant in the 6 Hz test and lowered total PDH by 23% in mice without status epilepticus; PDH activity was 65% lower in chronic epileptic mice and only partly restored.

[favourable, isoform-specific, disease-model astrocyte] PDK2 knockdown by siRNA in neonatal SOD1G93A rat astrocytes lowered PDH phosphorylation, restored mitochondrial parameters and increased the astrocytes' support of motor-neuron survival; the abstract declares PDK2 'low' in neurons, whereas the mouse P7 neuron value (13.75 FPKM) is not below the astrocyte value (17.27). [V2 correction: the abstract's 'PDK2 low in neurons' is not contradicted by the mouse P7 table (different species, age and metric; a 20 percent difference between two pools each); independent data cut against the abstract: 11197747 (PDK2 mRNA the most abundant isoform in rat brain regions) and 37188779 (neuron-specific PDK2 silencing in vivo, mouse), both abstract level; so 'no isoform-selective loss was found in neurons' is not supported]

[unfavourable: harm direction, peripheral glia] DCA reduced myelin proteins in a dose- and exposure-dependent manner in rat Schwann cell and DRG neuron myelinating co-cultures, with only partial recovery after washout; the held MELAS trial of DCA stopped for peripheral neuropathy. No CNS oligodendrocyte-lineage test of PDK loss or DCA was found in the strings run.

[neutral to null] In EAE mouse brain the DCA salt called a PDK4 inhibitor given alone did not change disability scores or cytokines; EAE alone raised active PDC activity (about 10.3 against 5.4 munits/mg, 8 mice per group, Fig 7 viewed) without changing PDK4; melatonin raised PDK4 about 2-fold and lowered PDC activity; the combination restored PDC activity and improved scores. This is a drug interaction in whole-brain homogenate, not a PDK4 loss.

[favourable, cell line] PDK4 siRNA in the mouse BV2 microglial line lowered M1 markers (N=3) and DCA lowered NLRP3-pyroptosis readouts in BV2 and in LPS-treated mice; PDK4 immunosignal in Iba1-positive cells rose with LPS. A line, not primary microglia; PDK1-PDK3 comparison was in blood monocytes, not brain.

[symbol trap, INFERENZA at title level] PDK1 is an HGNC alias of PDPK1 (HGNC:8816), the 3-phosphoinositide-dependent kinase. Ten of 25 PubMed hits for (PDK2 OR PDK4 OR PDK1) AND (knockout OR knockdown) AND neural terms read as PDPK1 work (conditional deletion in forebrain, Purkinje cells, interneurons, oligodendrocytes; three titles name pS6/PKC-gamma, PKB/GSK-3-beta or FoxO1); none opened. A 'PDK1 knockout in oligodendrocytes' paper is not evidence on the pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase without its abstract.
